About
ASCERTAIN
ASCERTAIN (Affordability and Sustainability improvements through new pricing, Cost- Effectiveness and ReimbursemenT models to Appraise INnovative health technologies) seeks to promote access to affordable technologies, the need to stimulate innovation and entrepreneurship, and the need to consider the environmental impact of innovations. Guided by a conceptual framework integrating pricing, health technology assessment and reimbursement/ payment, ASCERTAIN will develop open-access, easy to use, policy-supporting tools including pricing models and value assessment models, it addresses the need of patients, physicians, payers, regulators, and manufacturers to improve the affordability and accessibility to innovative health technologies (including pharmaceuticals) in Europe.
Tools will be tested for three use cases
ASCERTAIN aims to enhance current methods of (value-based) pricing, cost-effectiveness modeling, threshold-setting, reimbursement, and payment, to set affordable prices, and to facilitate a cyclic assessment of broader societal benefits including costs and risks. It seeks to find a sustainable balance and reimbursement models, which will be adaptable to country-specific conditions.

ASCERTAIN project for better pricing and reimbursement models enters final phase
The ASCERTAIN project is entering its final phase, with the final conference taking place on October 21, 2026 in Brussels.
ASCERTAIN – Affordability and Sustainability improvements through new pricing, Cost- Effectiveness and ReimbursemenT models to Appraise INnovative health technologies – is an EU funded project focused on improving the affordability and accessibility of innovative health technologies by developing a policy support tool. EHA is a consortium partner in the project, which aligns with our advocacy priority to promote affordable and equitable access to innovative therapies in hematology.
Accessibility and pricing of new health technologies in hematology
High prices of new health technologies impede access to treatments for many patients with blood disorders. Health systems face the challenge of facilitating patient access to new health technologies while ensuring the system’s financial sustainability and providing incentives for innovation. Together with Myeloma Patients Europe and patient organizations for PNH and Sickle Cell Disease, EHA is representing the hematology field in the development of the ASCERTAIN project.
The ASCERTAIN policy support tool
The ASCERTAIN policy support tool aims to contribute to better anticipating and calculating pricing, health technology assessment (HTA), and reimbursement conditions for innovative health technologies (IHTs).
